package: sea-orm-cli (entity generation only, no diagram output)
notes: Actively maintained ORM with a CLI that generates Rust entity code from a database, but no ERD/diagram renderer of its own — confirmed no dedicated visualization output exists as of 2026-07-06.

package: diesel (schema introspection only, no diagram output)
notes: Same gap as sea-orm: diesel print-schema / diesel_cli produce Rust structs, not an ERD. No community-maintained diesel-to-ERD crate was found in search as of 2026-07-06.

package: graphviz-rust (dot-file generation, then external Graphviz render)
notes: Fallback path: hand-build a .dot AST in Rust from schema metadata, then shell out to Graphviz for rendering. Workable but requires writing custom glue code — there is no off-the-shelf 'Rust ERD package' equivalent to Python's eralchemy2 or Node's mermaid-cli.

package: (gap) shell out to mermaid-cli / d2 from Rust via std::process::Command
notes: Realistically the best option for a Rust-based service today: emit Mermaid/D2 text from Rust schema structs, invoke the external CLI as a subprocess. Recorded as a 'gap' entry — Rust is the weakest language of the seven researched for this specific use case as of 2026-07-06.
